name: application-mobile-list-section
title: Mobile List Section
description: An iOS-style inset grouped list with an uppercase section header, rounded card container, divided rows, and trailing chevrons or value text — single-section and multi-section stacked variants.
useWhen: Building a settings or preferences screen with a native-feeling, iOS-style grouped list appearance.
Grouping several related navigation rows under a labeled section, with more than one section stacked on the same screen.
avoidWhen: You need a persistent sidebar navigation structure rather than a scrollable grouped list — a settings nav list or side menu is a better fit for that layout.
Rows need complex controls (multi-field forms, embedded charts) rather than simple navigation/value display — a plain list or table serves that better.
responsiveBehavior: The section header and rounded row group share consistent horizontal padding at any width; multiple sections stack vertically with generous gap so the grouping stays visually clear on any screen size.
accessibility: Each row is a real <a> (or button, if it's an action rather than navigation), keyboard-focusable and operable without relying on touch.
The chevron icon is decorative (aria-hidden); the row's own text conveys that it navigates further, following standard mobile list conventions.
Destructive rows (e.g. Sign out) are distinguished by explicit red text, not position or icon alone.

variants.title: Single section
variants.description: One grouped section (Account) with three rows, including a trailing value ('On') on the last row
accessibility: Each row is a real, keyboard-focusable link.

variants.title: Single section (Dark)
variants.description: One grouped section (Account) with three rows, including a trailing value ('On') on the last row
accessibility: Colors meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.

variants.title: Multiple sections
variants.description: Two stacked grouped sections (General, Support), the second including a destructive Sign out row
accessibility: The destructive Sign out row uses explicit red text, not position or icon alone.
